title: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Nexus 9000 Switches [CVE-2026-20212]: Unauthenticated RCE with Root Access
content_md:
Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Nexus 9000 Switches [CVE-2026-20212]: Unauthenticated RCE with Root Access

Cisco published a security bulletin describing a critical vulnerability in Nexus 9000 series switches based on Silicon One chipsets. The vulnerability, assigned CVE-2026-20212, carries a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8 (Critical). It allows an unauthenticated user to execute code remotely with root privileges. Security patches are available and immediate software updates are recommended.

The vulnerability stems from open access to a network service on TCP ports 43210 and 43211 in the default L3 VRF instance. Establishing a connection requires no authentication, and transmitted data is interpreted as code and executed with root privileges. Exploitation can cause the S1HAL process to crash, resulting in device restart. The vulnerability is classified as CWE-1327: Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address.

The main issue is not an authentication implementation bug but the exposure of the Silicon One service on ports where it should not be reachable, especially from outside the network. A potential attacker needs no Cisco account, credentials, or prior access to the switch. They only need to connect to the device on one of these ports and send crafted data directly to the exposed service.

Cisco confirmed that this attack vector allows complete device takeover. At the time of publication, Cisco PSIRT reported no observed exploitation in the wild or public disclosure. Affected product IDs include N9324C-SE1U, N9348Y2C6D-SE1U, N9364E-SG2-O, N9364E-SG2-Q, N9396T12C-SE1, N9348Y12C-SE1, N9396Y12C-SE1, N9336C-SE1, N9K-C9804, and N9K-C9808. Vulnerable NX-OS versions range from 10.3(1) to 10.6(3s). If patching is not immediately possible, Cisco recommends restricting access via iACL and deploying Live Protect.
